check.population: every generator, reflective access, evaluation site and language definition in the codebase
check.freshness: a verdict stands until a generator, a grammar or the model it generates from changes
check.refusal: the banned-API rule, the generator test or the grammar validation fails the change
check.observation: eval and reflection call sites read from source, and generated output compared with its model
check.evidence: none: the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it
check.authority: the model and the grammar, which generated output is derived from and compared against

distinctFrom.reason: Homoiconicity is programs held as data, while readability is how easily the developer reads the source that results.

records.name: Homoiconicity
records.definition: The degree to which a language represents its programs in its own data structures, so programs can be inspected and transformed as data.

exemplar.before:
function evaluateFoo(foo: Foo) { return foo.value * 2; }
const fooRule = { operation: "multiply", operand: 2 };

records.name: Code as Data
records.definition: A design rule that logic to be generated or transformed is held as a typed data structure, such as a syntax tree, that tools can inspect and rewrite.

exemplar.before: function fooRule(foo: Foo) { return foo.count > 3 && foo.active; }

distinctFrom.reason: Metaprogramming is code that writes or transforms code, while a domain-specific language is a notation for one domain, which metaprogramming can build.

records.name: Metaprogramming
records.definition: A technique for writing programs that generate or transform other programs, at compile time or at runtime.

exemplar.before:
class FooDto { id!: string; name!: string; }
class BarDto { id!: string; name!: string; }

distinctFrom.reason: Reflection reads type metadata at runtime, while dynamic binding selects an implementation at runtime, with or without reflection.
Introspection only reads a type and its members, while reflection also acts on what it reads.
Reflection inspects structure while the program runs, while static analysis inspects source without running it.

records.name: Reflection
records.definition: A mechanism that lets a program read and act on type metadata about its own structure at runtime.

exemplar.before:
const fields = ["id", "name", "count"];
for (const field of fields) renderField(foo[field]);

records.name: Introspection
records.definition: A mechanism that lets a program query an object's type and public members at runtime without changing them.

records.name: Compile-Time Evaluation
records.definition: A mechanism that computes values, checks or generated code during the build, so the work and its errors happen before runtime.

exemplar.after:
const fooRoutes = compileTime(() => buildRoutes(fooRouteDefinitions));
export const routeTable = fooRoutes;

records.name: Runtime Code Generation
records.definition: A mechanism that builds executable code while the program runs, from a specification such as a field mapping.

records.name: Domain-Specific Language (DSL)
records.definition: A design pattern that expresses a domain's rules or workflows in a small language with a defined grammar and a validator.

distinctFrom.reason: Language-oriented programming gives each domain its own language, while general-purpose code writes every domain in one language.

records.name: Language-Oriented Programming
records.definition: An approach in which each problem domain gets its own language, with a type checker and an evaluator, and solutions are written in it.

distinctFrom.reason: Model-driven architecture generates the implementation from a formal model by transformation rules, while metadata-driven design drives forms, routes or plugins from validated metadata.

records.name: Model-Driven Architecture
records.definition: An approach in which a formal model is the source of truth and the implementation is generated from it by transformation rules.
